subject.summary: The Invoices list in Ledgerly's web app, the page finance staff open daily to find, chase and close unpaid invoices.

theme.source: src/tokens.css (exact custom properties) and src/invoices.html (component styles)
theme.summary: Light theme on a pale sage ground (#f7f8f6) with white surfaces and hairline borders; one teal accent (#0f766e) for the current page and primary action; semantic status colours (paid green, due amber, overdue red, draft grey) as soft pills with text. Inter for UI, JetBrains Mono for invoice numbers and money; 12-26px type scale, 4px spacing steps, 6/10/14px radii, two soft shadows. Calm, terse business voice: Invoice, Client, Due, Overdue, Drafts, Send reminder, Mark paid.

must_keep: Ledgerly shell: the teal mark and Ledgerly wordmark, and navigation to Overview, Invoices (current), Clients, Payments, Reports, Settings
Totals: Outstanding, Overdue, Paid this month and Drafts, with today's values
Filter by status: All, Due, Overdue, Paid, Drafts, each with a live count
Search by client name or invoice number
Sort by invoice number, client, issued date, due date and amount, both directions
Every invoice shows its number, client, issued date, due date, status and amount in USD
Select one, several or all shown invoices, see how many are selected, then Send reminders, Mark paid or Clear
Per-invoice actions: View, Send reminder, Mark paid, Duplicate (as a draft), Delete
Export CSV of the current view
New invoice: client from the client list, amount above 0, due date, with inline messages; Save draft or Create & send; Cancel
No-match state with Clear filters (resets status and search)
Confirmation for every action, announced to screen readers
Keyboard: every control reachable with visible focus; Escape closes menus and the new-invoice panel
Brand: teal accent, Inter and JetBrains Mono, light theme, status colours with text labels, calm terse voice and today's terms
Usable on a phone (390 wide): navigation, filters, invoices and actions all reachable
may_change: derived views of existing data (days late, age, per-client balances)
constraints: Desktop web at 1440x900, usable down to 390 wide
WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and keyboard access, no worse than today
Light theme and Ledgerly tokens; no new colours for brand roles
No new capabilities or data beyond what the page has today (derived views of the same data are fine)

rounds.question: How should finance staff find what to chase today?
rounds.title: Ten ways to find what needs chasing
rounds.summary: Every option shows the same 18 invoices with today's totals and keeps every function on the page: status filters with counts, search, five sorts, bulk reminders and mark paid, the row menu, Export CSV and New invoice with its checks. What varies is what leads and how you get to the invoices that need chasing, from a re-weighted table to a one-at-a-time chase queue. Every frame is live: filter, sort, select, open menus and the New invoice panel; use the State menu for long values or no invoices. Reminders, export and navigation are simulated with a confirmation.

options.name: Lateness in view
options.idea: Today's page on its best day, re-weighted so overdue reads loudest: days late under every due date, a red Overdue total with a Show overdue button, and a visible Remind button on unpaid rows.
options.description: Same page and order as today; every due date now says how late it is, overdue totals and amounts are louder, and unpaid rows get a Remind button. Smallest change, but staff still scan a mixed list sorted by issue date.
options.cost: Still a mixed list; finding what to chase relies on reading the red text.
options.keeps: all contract items in today's positions; issue-date order; drawer for New invoice
options.changes: days late under due dates; Overdue total emphasised with Show overdue; inline Remind on unpaid rows; readable dates; sort arrows; selection sum in the bulk bar
